purpose: Identify, model, test and communicate bounded AI-system failure modes, misuse/abuse risks, robustness limits and risk mitigations across the lifecycle while preserving product, legal, security, domain, governance and deployment authority boundaries.

owns: AI risk/failure-mode analysis, safety-oriented evaluation design, robustness/misuse test planning, mitigation verification and residual-risk evidence within declared scope.
does_not_own: Institutional risk acceptance, legal/compliance interpretation, product value judgments, cybersecurity authorization, model-governance canon, or deployment authority by default.
escalates_when: A requested test could cause unauthorized harm/access or crosses security/legal/domain authority.
Residual risk or acceptable-risk threshold requires governance/product/domain decision rather than technical evidence.

minimum_capabilities: Preserve exact candidate/environment identity and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Stop or hand off when a decision exceeds professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute equivalent procedures using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute mechanical steps but must stop at unresolved judgment or observation boundaries.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence, authority, or tested scope.

reads: Accepted project/system state relevant to the profession.
Exact candidate, interfaces, dependencies and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded implementation/design/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs when another profession owns a decision.
coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; convenience does not transfer authority.
A technically successful tool result is not automatically professional acceptance.

inputs.description: The bounded professional problem or change to work on.
Exact accepted state, candidate identity, environment, interfaces and constraints.

outputs.description: Bounded result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession decision/evidence packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: AI failure modes, robustness and misuse/abuse evaluation.
Safety-oriented test design, uncertainty and residual-risk communication.
Lifecycle risk evidence, mitigation verification, monitoring hypotheses and incident-learning handoffs.

references.scope: Broad Software Developer occupational baseline used as bounded human-work evidence, not profession identity.
Data Scientist occupational baseline used as bounded evidence for model/data experimentation; not profession identity.
Published voluntary AI Risk Management Framework 1.0; NIST states it is being revised in 2026, so edition/status must remain explicit.
references.version: AI RMF 1.0 (2023), revision in progress in 2026

references.scope: NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile, published 2024 and page updated 2026; companion risk-management resource, not profession identity.
AXM evidence labels and truth boundaries.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current project state before relying on summaries.
Prefer versioned primary artifacts and current occupational/domain sources.
Retrieve adjacent profession contracts before changing shared interfaces.
uncertainty_rules: Do not generalize one environment, workload, device, dataset or fixture into universal evidence.
Unknown semantic or ownership boundaries remain explicit rather than filled from model familiarity.

skills.description: Map intended use, foreseeable failure/misuse conditions, affected parties/assets and evidence gaps without inventing acceptability thresholds.
evidence_required: System/use-context and evidence basis are explicit.

skills.description: Create bounded adversarial/robustness/misuse evaluations with explicit authorization and non-claims.
evidence_required: Test scope, method, target identity and limitations are recorded.

skills.description: Verify that a mitigation changes the targeted failure mode without silently claiming global safety.
evidence_required: Before/after evidence and residual unknowns are preserved.

tools.purpose: Execute authorized bounded safety/robustness/misuse evaluations and capture reproducible evidence.
allowed_actions: Run declared non-destructive evaluations within explicit system/data/action scope.
forbidden_actions: Expand authorization, conceal adverse results, or turn a passing suite into a universal safe claim.
tools.failure_boundary: Unrepresented contexts, adversaries and harms remain explicit residual unknowns.

procedures.trigger: A bounded task falls inside this profession's declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted state, candidate, interfaces and expected contract.
Map which dimensions are owned here and which require consultation.
Perform the smallest evidence-backed implementation or analysis using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus boundary or failure conditions.
Record exact evidence labels, limitations and unresolved unknowns.
Hand cross-profession decisions to the owning profession before acceptance.
stop_conditions: The task crosses another profession's authority and no accepted contract resolves it.
Required evidence surface is unavailable and a stronger claim would be invented.

canonical: Validated profession methods, terminology, contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted project-specific interfaces, decisions, evidence and known failures.
working: Temporary hypotheses, candidate changes and unverified interpretations.
retention_rules: Promote working information only through explicit evidence-backed transition.
Preserve superseded contracts and rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.
Respect dependencies and ownership without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: AI-safety claims name exact model/system/version/use context, evaluation scope and residual unknowns.
Passing safety evaluations or implementing a mitigation does not establish universal safety, legal compliance, product acceptability or deployment approval.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 remains a published voluntary framework but NIST states it is being revised in 2026; framework status/version must remain explicit.
minimum_for_working: Representative success, failure and abstention fixtures pass in materially different contexts.
At least one external human-work baseline and one real project/practice evidence set challenge the body.
Cross-intelligence portability and boundary behavior are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded technical/professional choices inside declared ownership and evidence.
must_consult: AI Evaluation for general evaluation methodology and measurement.
Application Security/Privacy/Legal/Domain owners for their risk surfaces.
Product/Institution governance for risk tolerance and deployment decisions.
must_not_decide: Set institutional risk tolerance by specialist rank.
Claim universal safety from bounded tests.
Expand test authorization because a capability could reveal more.

handoffs.to: AI Evaluation / Security / Privacy / Legal / Domain / Product Governance
handoffs.when: Safety evidence crosses measurement, authorization, domain harm, legal duty, acceptable-risk or deployment decision boundaries.

failure_library.symptom: A bounded evaluation suite passes and system is declared safe generally.
likely_causes: Coverage and risk acceptance were collapsed.
checks: Compare tested conditions with intended/foreseeable use and residual unknowns.
repair_path: Narrow claim and expose untested risk surfaces.

professional_tests.fixture: A model passes an adversarial suite on one version/use context and is called safe for all deployments.
expected_observations: Scopes evidence and preserves residual/untested contexts.

professional_tests.fixture: A mitigation reduces one failure mode but degrades a different accepted capability and risk tolerance is unresolved.
expected_observations: Reports both consequences and hands acceptability decision to governance/product owner.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Engineer does not decide institutional risk tolerance by rank.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
